answer.text: Near-riskless profits from pricing inefficiencies between related securities or markets

explanation.text: The Logic: Arbitrage exploits pricing inefficiencies to generate near-risk-free profits (e.g., cash-futures, index-component). The Trap: Other strategies carry directional risk. Cross-Exam Context: Core absolute-return approach. Distributor's Pro-Tip: True arbitrage is rare; most 'arb' funds take residual risks — understand the spread.
